What's right: switching to ceil(p/100*n) with 1-based indexing, handling p == 0, and adding the 0 <= p <= 100 check all match the docstring and fix the real bugs.

Blocking: the `p == 50 and n % 2 == 0` branch that averages the two middle values exists only to make test_median_response_time pass. The PR description admits this. It goes against the docstring, which the teammate named as the source of truth ("values are never averaged or interpolated"), and against the README ("every reported value is a real sample"). The PR then rewrote the docstring to cover the hack, which reverses the requested priority. It also changes behavior users will see: latency_summary's p50 would show a value that was never sampled whenever the batch size is even, and the method would jump only at exactly p=50.

Please remove the special case and restore the original docstring. Leave test_median_response_time failing (nearest rank gives 120) and raise it with the teammate as a test that contradicts the spec. We shouldn't bend the implementation to fit it.

Minor: `p / 100 * n` can overshoot a whole number because of float rounding. For example, 0.7*10 == 7.000000000000001, so ceil gives rank 8 when it should be 7. Using `math.ceil(p * n / 100)` avoids this for integer inputs.
